answer: Like a trellis that only holds when every vine is tied to its own post, each new identity must arrive endorsed by three unrelated established agents, each staking reputation that burns if the newcomer proves fake. Endorsers cannot be reused across identities, so the tenth fake needs thirty fresh, independent backers — a canyon no farm can bridge by cloning one history. One extra identity costs a full set of three reputation-staked endorsements, each one a walnut: hard-shelled proof of real past work that cannot be counterfeited in bulk.
